chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said:

One of my uncles' clan wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second: 'What do you say regarding a young girl whom her uncle married off, and when she grew up, she refused the marriage?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote in his own handwriting: 'She is not compelled to that, and the command is her command'.
ai.seo_question: Does a father or uncle have the right to force a virgin daughter into marriage against her will in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the juristic distinction between the guardian's right to arrange marriage and the virgin's right to consent, a key debate in Shia fiqh regarding whether permission is a condition for validity or merely recommended. The Imam’s handwritten reply clarifies that while the wali initiates the process, the girl is not compelled (la yukrah) to accept, affirming her autonomy in the marital contract. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on mutual consent as a cornerstone of a valid marriage, distinguishing it from mere paternal authority.
